personality_one_liner: A calm, watchful protector — like a premium consumer-security product (Norton / Malwarebytes / 1Password Watchtower tier), not a hacker-black antivirus. Bright, clean, neutral surfaces with strong navy structure; amber/green/orange/red are reserved for Apollo's security states so colour always means something. Apollo himself — an animated guard dog — is the brand, not a shield icon.

spacing.rule: 8pt grid. Generous outer margins for cards, tight grouping for internal metadata. No dense information walls — Home in particular must read as a small number of clear, scannable blocks, not a long form.

icon_set: lucide-react-native (@react-native-vector-icons is not used; do not introduce Phosphor, FontAwesome or other icon families)

glassmorphism.note: No blur/glass effects anywhere. Depth comes from white cards (surfaceSecondary) on the #F5F7FA neutral background plus a 1px border (colors.border), not from translucency.

platform_libraries.image: expo-image (GIF playback for the animated Apollo hero — see apollo_hero below)

apollo_hero.rule: Apollo is an animated character, not a static shield icon — this is core brand identity and must never be replaced with a static illustration.

assets.ears_up: assets/images/apollo-ears-up.gif — NOT YET PROVIDED, falls back to the static assets/images/logo.png mark until this asset is added. Selection lives in a single state→asset map in ApolloHero.tsx so dropping the file in is a one-line change.
assets.biting: assets/images/apollo-barking.gif (shares the barking GIF; ring/glow intensity escalates further in code)

apollo_hero.size: ~170px on standard phones (largest single element on Home), scaling down slightly only on very small/narrow devices. Never cropped.
apollo_hero.background_treatment: The hero card itself stays mostly white (surfaceSecondary). The current state's colour appears only as a restrained pulsing glow/ring directly behind Apollo — never as a full-card gradient or tint wash. Apollo and the state wording carry the personality, not the card background.
apollo_hero.state_progression: Patrolling (resting) → Sniffing → Ears Up → Growling → Barking → Biting is Apollo's visual threat-escalation ladder and must always read as increasing attention/seriousness. Do not alter the underlying state-machine logic to fit visuals — visuals follow the existing Truth-of-State resolution, never the reverse.

dev_mode_presentation.rule: The mock-adapter indicator (shown when isMock is true) must remain present for QA (keep its test IDs and underlying logic), but must read as a small, muted, secondary tag — never a bright/colourful badge competing with Apollo or the state colours. Use a small pill/text tag in surfaceTertiary with onSurfaceSecondary text, tucked into a header corner.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: A bright, compact dashboard: Apollo's current state as the dominant element, then the most-used checks, a compact protection/verification summary, and a short recent-activity glance — not a long capability table.

states.loading: Neutral #F5F7FA screen; hero card shows a soft state-coloured glow behind a static Apollo mark while data loads.
states.empty: Apollo resting/patrolling; Recent Patrol shows the calm 'All quiet — Apollo is patrolling within the checks he can see.' state, no illustration needed.
states.error: Compact banner card: 'Connection interrupted' with a neutral border and a retry action; does not block the rest of Home.

screens.layout: 1) Header: 'Apollo' title + logo, dev-mode tag de-emphasised (see dev_mode_presentation). 2) Apollo Hero (see apollo_hero) with state title, one-line meaning, reason, Hear Higgins, and visibility/status chips — compact, not a wall of text. 3) Quick Checks: four icon tiles for the most-used checks (Check a link, Check a message, Check this call, Scan a code) in a single row, plus an 'All checks' expander revealing the remaining checks (file, app, device, network, account, email) as the same tile style — every existing route stays reachable. 4) Protection summary + Verification: two compact cards ('N active · N need attention' → Manage in Guard; 'Last verified HH:MM' → Verify now). Stacked vertically on phones; side-by-side only at tablet/wide widths. 5) Connected events (Threat Scent) when present. 6) Recent Patrol: latest 2–3 events max, 'See all' → Patrol tab. 7) This week: one small, secondary digest card below Recent Patrol — Patrol remains the primary home for history, not this card.

screens.name: Guard
screens.purpose: The detailed protection-management screen: every capability, its permission, and network/account sub-guards.

states.loading: Skeleton rows reflecting the card-list layout.
states.empty: Not applicable — capabilities are always a fixed known set.
states.error: Compact retry banner above the capability list.

screens.layout: Master protection card (Requested/Enforcement/Verified truth pills) at top. Network Guard and Account Guard summary cards. Then one card per capability: small icon in a tinted circle + title + one-line explanation + status pill (Active/Permission required/Unsupported/Coming later) + a chevron only when the row is actionable (permission_required). Never show green for an unknown/unsupported/coming-later status — those stay neutral grey. Permissions list and Connection/Wi‑Fi trust section below.

screens.name: Check a Link
screens.purpose: A dedicated utility to manually paste and scan a URL for threats, delivering a clear risk verdict.

states.loading: Scanning line sweep over the URL container.
states.empty: Clean input field with a prominent 'Paste link' action, centered.
states.error: Invalid URL format or network failure message.

screens.layout: Single-column utility layout. Large form input at top. Results appear in a state-tinted card below (amber for growling/ears_up, red for barking/biting, green for resting) with clear next actions.

screens.name: Patrol
screens.purpose: A chronological timeline of security events showing exactly what Apollo did, marked by state colours.

states.loading: Skeleton of the timeline rail and event cards.
states.empty: 'All quiet — Apollo is patrolling within the checks he can see.'
states.error: Failed to load timeline events, subtle retry action.

screens.layout: Sticky date groupings. A vertical rail with a state-coloured dot per event; cards to the right. Tapping opens a detail sheet (What happened / Why / What to do).

screens.name: Ask Higgins
screens.purpose: A chat interface where Higgins (Apollo's handler, speaking in the first person) explains events and answers security questions in plain English — never decides what is safe.

states.empty: Just the suggestion chips and input bar — no large intro card; Higgins is already introduced elsewhere (onboarding/settings).
states.error: Inline 'I couldn't answer right now.' message, first person.

screens.layout: Standard chat layout. Apollo/Higgins messages in a tinted bubble, user messages in a plain bubble. Recommended-check chips render inline under a Higgins reply. Input pinned above the keyboard.

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Controls for privacy, data egress, family, and app configuration.
screens.layout: Grouped list layout. Sections for Privacy, Data Controls, Family, About. The mock-adapter dev label appears subtly at the bottom (see dev_mode_presentation), never as a headline element.

instructions_to_main_agent: Single bright theme (Light Sentinel) — do not add a dark mode or reintroduce dark-navy/black surfaces. surface (#F5F7FA) + surfaceSecondary (#FFFFFF) + a 1px border (colors.border) is the entire depth system; no glassmorphism, no heavy gradients, no glow-behind-everything.
Use 'Outfit' for all headings/state titles, 'Geist' for body text and metadata — unchanged from before.

Never colour a whole screen or card in a state colour. State colour (sniffing/resting/ears_up/growling/barking/biting from the theme) is reserved for: the Apollo hero's glow/ring, status pills/dots, and result cards on check screens. Everything else stays neutral (surface/surfaceSecondary/onSurface/onSurfaceSecondary).
Apollo's animated GIF (see apollo_hero) is mandatory on Home and must stay the single most visually prominent element — never shrink it below icon-sized or replace it with a static shield.
capabilityTone() must never map an unsupported/unknown/coming-later status to green (already correct in code — do not regress this).

Bottom navigation is a light bar: white background, navy (#162235-family) inactive icons/labels, Apollo amber (#F4B942) active tab. Keep all five tabs (Home, Guard, Patrol, Higgins, Settings) and safe-area handling on both Android and iOS.
Use lucide-react-native icons exclusively. Do not introduce Phosphor or any other icon family.
No indigo, violet, or purple hues. Stick exactly to the provided palette.
Never display emoji in the UI.
Do not hard-code colours inside screens/components — always read from theme.ts tokens via useTheme()/makeStyles(), matching the color block above exactly.

This is a visual/layout system, not a security-logic change: preserve all existing routes, test IDs, Truth-of-State semantics (Requested ≠ Operational ≠ Verified), and the 6-state behaviour model exactly as implemented.
